findings.title: A credential from user storage can now be passed to `removeStoredCredentialById`, which only works on the local store.
findings.body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns the user-storage credential first. When that credential's codes are all used, the next lines call `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. That method only deletes from the local Keycloak DB.

For a user-storage credential the id is not a local id and can be null. The test provider's `getCredentials` builds the model with `createFromValues`, which sets no id. So once the last code is used, one of two things happens:
- the delete silently does nothing, and the credential stays in user storage;
- or the local store rejects a null id, and the login fails at that point.

I could not see how the JPA store handles a null id.

**Fix:** only call `removeStoredCredentialById` when the credential came from local storage. For user-storage credentials, ask the provider to remove or disable them instead, for example with `disableCredentialType`.

findings.title: `getCredentials` throws a NullPointerException when the user is not in the provider's map.
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null; other methods in this class, such as `isConfiguredFor` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, check for that. The new `getCredentials` reads `myUser.recoveryCodes` directly, so a call for a user that is not in `users` throws a NullPointerException. Add `if (myUser == null) return Stream.empty();`.
